Notebook.Title: Fork: Process Trees, cgroups, and PID Reuse

Section.Title: Welcome
Section.Paragraph: Both cells below share Scope="fork", so they compile and run together as one program: the first cell creates world once, and the second cell reuses it plus every type the first cell declared. Press Run on the second cell to see both scenes; press Run on the first alone to see just the container-image scene.

Section.Title: Scene 1: fork() From a Container Image
Section.Paragraph: [SiaBundle] groups several components into one shape you can add or remove as a unit — world.Create().AddBundle(new ContainerImage()) stamps out a process with Process, Owner, and Sandboxed all at once, and RemoveBundle<ProcessImage>() strips a matching subset back off, returning whatever it removed.

Section.Title: Scene 2: pstree, cgroups, and /proc
Section.Paragraph: Hierarchy<ProcessTree> tracks parent/child links (with a cgroup-style "freeze this subtree" flag), Aggregator<Uid> groups entities by a shared key so ProcessCountByOwnerSystem can react whenever the group's membership changes, and Mapper<Pid> is a stable id -> entity lookup — like /proc/<pid> — that survives a destroyed entity's id being reassigned to a brand new one.
Both scenes ran as one program: Process, Uid, and the rest of Scene 1's types were declared in the first cell but used here, unqualified, with no re-declaration needed.
